parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module passes. All five files share one concern: wiring the application together. Dependencies.ts declares one `Dependencies` interface for the shared adapters (users, projects, tasks, ids). AppFactory.ts is the only place that creates the concrete adapters, and it builds that object once. Each feature module (ProjectModule.ts, TaskModule.ts, UserModule.ts) takes `deps: Dependencies`, builds its use cases from it and returns its controller's routes as an Express Router. No feature module creates its own repository or ID generator, so none of them bypasses the shared abstraction. Each use case is built in exactly one place, so no wiring rule is repeated. CreateTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase are built in ProjectModule because ProjectController uses them, which is consistent with routes scoped to a project. No file contains business rules or invariants that could be duplicated.
